batchName: Empire: Augustus and the Principate (27 BC-AD 14) - Easy Batch 1
chapterName: Empire: Augustus and the Principate (27 BC-AD 14)

questions.question: What did Rome do after the disaster in the Teutoburg Forest?
questions.explanation: The Varian Disaster marked the limit of Augustus's expansion, and Rome gave up conquest beyond the Rhine.
questions.sourceQuote: Rome abandoned conquest beyond the Rhine.

questions.question: Which office did Augustus give up on 1 July 23 BC after recovering from a grave illness?
questions.explanation: After nearly dying, Augustus gave up the consulship he had held every year. The Senate gave him even greater powers in its place.
questions.sourceQuote: He seemed to be dying, but he recovered and, on 1 July 23 BC, gave up the consulship.

questions.question: According to tradition, what did Augustus boast on his deathbed about Rome?
options: He found it at war and left it at peace
He found it small and left it vast
He found it poor and left it rich
He found it brick and left it marble
questions.explanation: Tradition says he claimed to have found Rome a city of brick and left it a city of marble. The boast had substance, as marble became a standard building material under him.
questions.sourceQuote: On his deathbed, according to tradition, Augustus boasted that he had found Rome a city of brick and left it a city of marble.

questions.question: Which of Augustus's names survived in later titles such as kaiser and czar?
questions.explanation: The title Caesar lived on as kaiser and czar. His legacy also included a professional army, a dynasty and a rebuilt capital.
questions.sourceQuote: Few deny his legacy: a professional army, a dynasty, a rebuilt capital, and titles such as Caesar that survived as kaiser and czar.

questions.question: Which position did Augustus take in 12 BC, making him head of Rome's state religion?
questions.explanation: In 12 BC he became chief priest, pontifex maximus. Ten years later the Senate also named him Father of the Fatherland.
questions.sourceQuote: In 12 BC he became chief priest (*pontifex maximus*), head of Rome's state religion.

questions.question: Which bodyguard did Augustus found in 27 BC that grew into a powerful force in Roman politics?
questions.explanation: The Praetorian Guard began as a bodyguard and grew into the emperor's household troops. Many of Augustus's institutions outlived him by centuries.
questions.sourceQuote: In 27 BC he founded the Praetorian Guard, a bodyguard that grew into the emperor's household troops and a powerful force in Roman politics.

questions.question: How did Christians in the Middle Ages view Augustus?
questions.explanation: Medieval Christians believed his reign prepared the world for Christ.
questions.sourceQuote: In the Middle Ages Christians saw him as a God-sent peacemaker whose reign prepared the world for Christ.

questions.question: What title did Augustus himself prefer to be called?
questions.explanation: Augustus preferred to be called the leading or first citizen, or princeps. The system he created is known as the Principate.
questions.sourceQuote: Augustus preferred to be called the leading or first citizen (*princeps*).

questions.question: Which month was renamed August in Augustus's honour in 8 BC?
questions.explanation: Sextilis became August, matching July, which was named for Julius Caesar.
questions.sourceQuote: In 8 BC the month Sextilis was renamed August in his honour, matching July, named for Julius Caesar.

questions.question: What was the birth name of the man who became Rome's first emperor?
questions.explanation: Rome's first emperor was born Gaius Octavius in 63 BC, into a comfortable but not famous family. Historians usually call him Octavian for the years 44 to 27 BC.
questions.sourceQuote: The man who became Rome's first emperor was born Gaius Octavius in 63 BC, into a comfortable but not famous family.
